correctness.rationale: The proof derives the exact nullities of all powers of the neighbor-sum matrix from a cyclic polynomial quotient and a parity-resolved rank-one perturbation, then applies the Fitting decomposition to count all initial states entering periodic dynamics by each time. The final-layer probability and density are direct substitutions. Independently written exact GF(2) rank and trajectory programs passed on 2,094 graph-size multisets and 83,136 binary initial configurations; finite checks are corroboration, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The invariant is directly motivated by transient durations and recurrent-state accessibility in network XOR dynamics. For a natural whole family of nearly complete graphs, the explicit formula describes every temporal layer and pinpoints precisely the cubic divisibility and two-adic source of nilpotent blocks. Deleting a vanishing edge proportion from a reversible even complete graph generates a sharp linear transient experienced by 15/16 of all binary configurations; this is a structurally meaningful counterexample to density-only transient heuristics, not a routine table or arbitrary parameter slice.
